rationale: The target verb is ko-matizo, an explicitly ko-prefixed present form, translated wakes one up. The Preterit base form is matəzle, also illustrated by the preceding example matəzle.

summary: No new tyz sense, Detransitive paradigm or example is published from the two uncertain JTM forms. The semantic observation is retained: kmiṭavəz describes a person freezing when pursuit reverses; ṭavizo describes a limp/stiff arm, without an expressed external agent.
The secure tayəz at 65/277 remains I Preterit Intransitive, with zero-marked brother as subject, m- sleep source and ʕal- sound trigger. It is already quoted.

The inherited III entry has matəzle/matəz base forms and two awakening examples but no sense gloss. Its coffee example komatizo is formally ko- plus an Infectum-like form although stored under Preterit; this inherited structural issue should not be concealed.
Allowed form lookups returned no exact attestation of kmiṭavəz or ṭavizo. The provisional reader root assignment is not independently corroborated.
Are kmiṭavəz (JTM 5.2/57) and ṭavizo (JTM 5.2/95) forms of a separate ṭvz/ṭwz verb, or dialect forms associated with tyz? Establish the root and stem before assigning a Detransitive sense.
Supply an editorial III gloss and determine the correct box for inherited komatizo in tyz.III.t.preterit.2. It appears to be Infectum rather than Preterit; no numbered III sense is invented here.
